instructions: Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.

In a large bowl, mix the ground pork with the maple syrup, onion powder, garlic powder, 2 tbsp minced sage, salt and pepper. Use your hands and stop as soon as it's evenly mixed. Any longer and the patties turn tough.
Scoop out about 2 tbsp of the mix at a time and press each into a patty about 2 1/2 inches wide. You should get about 20 patties. Set them on the baking sheet.
Set aside 8 patties for breakfast. Freeze the other 12 on the baking sheet until they're firm, about 1 hour.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large nonstick or cast iron skillet over medium heat.

Cook the 8 patties in a single layer, 4 minutes per side, until they're deep brown. Lower the heat if they brown too fast. The pork is cooked at 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Transfer the patties to a plate lined with paper towels. Serve warm, with the red pepper flakes on the table for anyone who wants heat.
Once the frozen patties are firm, transfer them to a freezer bag. They keep for 3 months. Cook them from frozen over medium heat for 5 minutes per side, until there's no pink in the middle.
Leftover cooked patties keep in the fridge for 3 to 4 days in an airtight container. Reheat them in a skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes per side.
method_notes: Cup of Yum leads: 5.0 from 82 ratings, 2 lbs of ground pork with maple syrup, onion and garlic powder, sage, salt, pepper and chili flakes, 4 minutes per side. A Spicy Perspective agrees on the mix and adds fennel and thyme, and gives the storage times used here: 3 to 4 days in the fridge, 3 months in the freezer. The chili flakes are moved to the table to keep the base mild. Written as a batch: cook 8 now and freeze the rest raw.
